title: Drafted for the First World War and the night of dime banks
summary: Dawson was drafted but a letter after the armistice said he was not qualified; on the eve of leaving he serenaded all night and spent his dimes.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: But anyway, what happened, what, did you go to Cuba and the Spanish and American War, anything?
Well, my dad and my father was, but I, I, uh, I, uh, uh,
You never did do any service?
I was drafted in that, uh, first, uh, that, uh, third world war, I think it was, uh, in 19... that was, that's before the war, war, war broke out in 19, 19, 1917. Uh-huh.
And you, and you were drafted?
I was drafted about, I think it must have been 15 or 16, in, for that war.
No, they sent me a note, you know when the armstick was signed?
That's when I got a letter, I was not qualified for military service. Mm-hmm.
And now your time? I was, I had, I had a, a letter about that long fixing to go away, had to go away the next morning.

But I had about five or six of them little dime banks, full of diamonds. And we serenaded that night, we had a good time, and I drank with all my, all my dimes up in there, and by the time I got, morning come for the, for the go away, there'll come there, the whistle blowing and everything, there'll come the messenger boy knocking on the door, thinking about, my nose, disqualified for military service.
Well you might have been too drunk anyway. Yeah. You might have had double diabetes or something, the time you finish that.
You know, we must have been fixed up, we had five or sixty. Dime banks. Oh, Dime banks. What about the Landrys?
